chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Barqi (may God have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Jamilah al-Mufaz'al ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nabata, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said:

Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon Adam (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Adam! I have been ordered to let you choose one of three things. Choose one and leave the other two.' Adam asked him: 'What are the three, O Gabriel?' He said: 'The intellect, shyness, and religion.' Adam said: 'I have chosen the intellect.' Gabriel said to shyness and religion: 'Return.' They said: 'O Gabriel! We are ordered to be with the intellect wherever it is.' Gabriel said: 'Then it is your concern,' and ascended.
ai.seo_question: What did Adam choose between intellect, shyness, and religion?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Khisal, Adam’s selection of intellect (al-'aql) as the primary faculty highlights its foundational role in Shia epistemology, where it serves as the vessel for both modesty (al-haya') and religion (al-din). This interconnection underscores the Shia scholarly view that true religious practice and moral character are inextricably linked to the proper application of reason, ensuring that faith is not merely ritualistic but deeply internalized and guided by insight.
